# ais-catcher

**AIS receiver and decoder for marine vessel traffic, with a web map**

- **Version recorded:** 0.70
- **Categories:** `sdr`, `tracking`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/jvde-github/AIS-catcher>

## What it does

Receives AIS transmissions from ships on 161.975 and 162.025 MHz using an SDR, decodes the position and identity messages, and plots the vessels on a web map served locally.

## Why you would want it

It is the most capable open AIS decoder available, and coastal monitoring is a natural companion to ADS-B aircraft tracking on the same receiver hardware.

## Before it will work

An RTL-SDR or similar receiver and a VHF marine-band antenna. You must be within range of the coast or inland waterways.

## How it installs

- git (cmake) — https://github.com/jvde-github/AIS-catcher at `v0.70`
  - build dependencies: `build-essential`, `cmake`, `pkg-config`, `libsoxr-dev`, `libsamplerate0-dev`, `librtlsdr-dev`, `libairspy-dev`, `libhackrf-dev`, `libcurl4-openssl-dev`, `zlib1g-dev`
  - Dependencies are declared rather than discovered, so `--dry-run` can show the whole set before anything is installed. AHRL's approach hides them inside a downloaded script.

Binaries this produces:

- `AIS-catcher`

## Known problems

Upstream's own installer downloads and executes a shell script. We do not use it: this manifest builds from a pinned git tag with declared dependencies so the install is inspectable before it runs.
